statement: Let M = 1000000007. Let N be the number of sets I subset of {0,...,len(nums)-1} such that, when the elements of I are written in increasing order as i_1 < ... < i_k, there exist positive integers p,q,s with k = p+q+s and: nums[i_j] = 0 for 1 <= j <= p; nums[i_j] = 1 for p < j <= p+q; nums[i_j] = 2 for p+q < j <= p+q+s. The function returns a result r (it does not fail) and r = N mod M.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] in {0,1,2}.

statement: The function returns a result r; it does not fail (no panic, out-of-bounds access, or 64-bit overflow occurs).
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] in {0,1,2}.

statement: The function returns a result r and 0 <= r < M, where M = 1000000007.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] in {0,1,2}.

statement: Let z = #{i | 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i]=0}, o = #{i | 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i]=1}, and t = #{i | 0 <= i < len(nums) and nums[i]=2}. The function returns a result r and r <= (2^z - 1)*(2^o - 1)*(2^t - 1). Here the right-hand side is an ordinary mathematical integer, not evaluated with 64-bit wrap-around.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] in {0,1,2}.

statement: The function returns a result r and r = 0.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] in {0,1,2}. There exists v in {0,1,2} such that for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] != v.

statement: The function returns a result r and r = 1 if nums[0]=0 and nums[1]=1 and nums[2]=2, and r = 0 otherwise.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] in {0,1,2}. len(nums) = 3.

statement: Let z, o, t be the numbers of occurrences of 0, 1, 2 in nums, respectively. The function returns a result r and r = ((2^z - 1)*(2^o - 1)*(2^t - 1)) mod 1000000007.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] in {0,1,2}. For every i,j with 0 <= i < j < len(nums), nums[i] <= nums[j].

statement: Let a be the smallest index with nums[a]=0 and b be the largest index with nums[b]=2. If a < b, then the function returns r and r = count_special_subsequences(nums[a..b]), where nums[a..b] is the slice containing exactly the indices a,a+1,...,b inclusive. If a > b, then the function returns r and r = 0.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] in {0,1,2}. There exists i with nums[i]=0 and there exists i with nums[i]=2.

statement: Let t = #{k | b < k < len(nums) and nums[k]=2}. The function returns a result r and r = (2^t - 1) mod 1000000007.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] in {0,1,2}. There is exactly one index a with nums[a]=0, there is exactly one index b with nums[b]=1, and a < b.

statement: Let z = #{i | 0 <= i < b and nums[i]=0}. The function returns a result r and r = (2^z - 1) mod 1000000007.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] in {0,1,2}. There is exactly one index b with nums[b]=1, there is exactly one index c with nums[c]=2, and b < c.

statement: Let o = #{i | a < i < c and nums[i]=1}. The function returns a result r and r = (2^o - 1) mod 1000000007.
preconditions: 1 <= len(nums) <= 100000 and for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums), nums[i] in {0,1,2}. There is exactly one index a with nums[a]=0, there is exactly one index c with nums[c]=2, and a < c.
